summary: mymatasan now notices when a camera stops seeing its scene. A new tamper monitor samples the frame the recorder already siphons for the AI detector and raises an alert when the lens is covered or sprayed, the camera has been knocked out of focus or turned to face somewhere else, or the picture has frozen while the connection stayed up. None of those were visible before: the health monitor asks whether the camera answers, and a covered lens answers fine; the continuity monitor asks whether footage is being written, and footage of a wall is still footage. This is what an attacker arranges before doing anything worth recording. No AI is involved — it is arithmetic over frames already being decoded (edge energy for a blocked view, frame-to-frame difference for a frozen picture, luma-histogram distance for a moved camera). Two decisions make it usable rather than noisy. Blocked-view checks are measured against each camera's OWN rolling median rather than an absolute threshold, so a busy loading bay and a plain corridor both work, and readings taken while a camera is already alerting are excluded from that baseline so a lens left covered cannot quietly become the new normal. And blocked-view checks pause automatically in low light, because a night scene loses detail on its own — without that, every camera in the fleet would report a covered lens at dusk and the feature would be muted by morning. The trade is explicit: a lens covered overnight is reported at first light. Tunable from Settings > Camera health; new metric mymatasan_camera_tamper_total by kind.
compatibility: Backward compatible, additive. New endpoints GET/PUT /api/settings/tamper; no schema changes and no migration. The monitor defaults to ON and only watches cameras that have recording enabled (it needs the siphon frame). Existing installs begin checking after upgrade. Not yet live-benched — in particular the overnight false-positive run, which is what decides whether the thresholds are right; see docs/FLAGSHIP_BENCH_CHECKLIST.md.
